claims.claim: Title: "9 exhibits, 127 figures, 3 of them wrong"
claims.source: Rounding Errors repository, reports/001-ireland through reports/009-nigeria
claims.passage: "claim": "From there it laundered upward, promoted in the United States by a former Surgeon General in the 1990s." ... "verdict": "NOT SUPPORTED"
claims.notes: 127 claim checks across 9 files is correct, but 1 of the '3 wrong' (007 claim 11) was rated NOT SUPPORTED for lack of a source, not shown wrong, and 007 now cites a source confirming it (see claim 18).

claims.claim: Ledger: Claims checked 127
claims.source: Rounding Errors repository, reports/001-ireland through reports/009-nigeria
claims.notes: Verdict entries per file: 20, 12, 14, 10, 11, 14, 13, 16, 17, which sum to 127.

claims.claim: Ledger: Fully supported by the exhibit's own cited sources 84
claims.source: Rounding Errors repository, reports/001-ireland through reports/009-nigeria
claims.passage: "claim": "The University of Michigan had already tried to reproduce Sandler's rabbit results in 1941 and failed.", "source": "Wikipedia, Benjamin P. Sandler (en.wikipedia.org)", ... "verdict": "SUPPORTED", "notes": "Fact confirmed by direct fetch, but the citation is to Wikipedia itself, which is a BLOCKING house-rule violation under SOURCING regardless of the claim's truth."
claims.notes: The SUPPORTED count is 84 (11+9+8+7+10+12+7+14+6), but the row label overstates it: 004 claim 6 is counted though its cited source was Wikipedia, and several others (002 claims 8 to 10, 004 claims 5, 7 to 9) were confirmed only through search caches after a 403.

claims.claim: Ledger: Not fully supported 43
claims.source: Rounding Errors repository, reports/001-ireland through reports/009-nigeria
claims.passage: "verdict": "PARTIALLY SUPPORTED" (29 entries across the 9 files); "verdict": "NOT SUPPORTED" (14 entries across the 9 files)

claims.claim: Ledger: Wrong on the facts 3
claims.source: Rounding Errors repository, reports/003-china and reports/007-10000-steps
claims.passage: "notes": "The listed source has no URL and names no individual; independent search found no primary documentation of a 1990s Surgeon General promotion of the '10,000 steps' figure specifically, and the one well-documented Surgeon General walking initiative (\"Step It Up!\") dates to 2015, which cuts against the claim as stated."
claims.notes: 003 claims 9 and 10 were wrong on timing, but 007 claim 11 was unsourced rather than shown false, and 007's current text sources it to Shape Up America!, founded 1994 by former Surgeon General C. Everett Koop, so the count of factual errors that hold up is 2.

claims.claim: ledgerNote: "The 3 were 2 dates in exhibit 003"
claims.source: Rounding Errors repository, reports/003-china
claims.passage: "notes": "The 40% figure is correct, but the timing is wrong: Inner Mongolia's admission came in January 2018, about a year after Liaoning's, not 'within weeks.'" ... "notes": "The one-third figure is correct, but this admission was made in January 2018, not within weeks of the January 2017 Liaoning confession."
claims.notes: 003 claims 9 and 10 are both NOT SUPPORTED on timing alone.

claims.claim: ledgerNote: "and 1 attribution in 007, all since fixed"
claims.source: Rounding Errors repository, reports/007-10000-steps; commit f0c49f4
claims.passage: "verdict": "NOT SUPPORTED", "notes": "The listed source has no URL and names no individual; independent search found no primary documentation of a 1990s Surgeon General promotion..."
claims.notes: The line was fixed, since 007 now names Koop and Shape Up America! with a source, but the fix shows the attribution was substantively right and only unsourced, so calling it an error on the facts is not supported.

claims.claim: ledgerNote and body: 16 claims marked partially supported because the cited source could not be retrieved (403, 503, a paywall, a corrupted file, or in 1 case no URL)
claims.source: Rounding Errors repository, reports/001-ireland through reports/009-nigeria
claims.passage: "notes": "CNN's page returned HTTP 503 on two direct fetch attempts..." / "both direct fetches of the Hollywood Reporter URL failed (403 then 402 paywall)" / "The linked BU Law Review PDF fetched as corrupted/garbled binary text" / "No URL is provided for this source" / "the listed source has no URL to verify directly"
claims.notes: 16 can be rebuilt (002-11; 003-6, 003-11; 005-11; 006-13; 007-1, 4, 9; 009-1, 2, 3, 4, 9, 10, 11, 13), but only by counting 009-11 and leaving out 004 claims 1 and 2, whose listed source also had no URL, which contradicts 'in 1 case'; the count depends on a classification the exhibit does not state.

claims.claim: ledgerNote and body: "8 claims were true, independently verifiable, and cited to nothing in the exhibit's own source list"
claims.source: Rounding Errors repository, reports/001-ireland and reports/002-argentina
claims.passage: "notes": "Plausible institutional fact (Eurostat validates EU national accounts) but no source in the list documents this specific sign-off for Ireland's 2015/2016 revision." ... "notes": "No source in the exhibit's list mentions provincial statistical offices; the claim is plausible and consistent with contemporaneous reporting but is not traceable to any of the six listed sources."
claims.notes: The 8 are 001 claims 4 to 10 plus 002 claim 7, but the reports call 2 of them only 'plausible' (001-8, 002-7), so only 6 were verified as true, and 001-5 was cited to a listed source that did not contain it rather than to nothing.

claims.claim: ledgerNote and body: "1 published source URL returned 404"
claims.source: Rounding Errors repository, reports/001-ireland
claims.passage: "notes": "That exact URL returns HTTP 404; the correct live URL uses 'glitter' not 'glitters' in the slug, meaning the published citation link is broken."
claims.notes: 001 claim 19 is NOT SUPPORTED for exactly this reason.

claims.claim: Verdict: "Rules broken: 1 of this museum's own. Every figure must trace to a source listed in the exhibit; 8 did not."
claims.source: Rounding Errors repository, reports/003-china, reports/006-dare, reports/004-icecream-polio
claims.passage: "notes": "The claim is true and independently verifiable (WikiLeaks cable 07BEIJING1760_a, reported by CNBC/VOA/Bloomberg), but the exhibit's sources list contains no citation for it at all, so within the exhibit's own paper trail this claim is uncited." ... "notes": "Confirmed true via independent web search (Britannica, CrimeSolutions/NIJ), but no entry in the exhibit's own sources list backs this specific date and origin, so it does not trace to a listed source as the FIGURES rule requires."
claims.notes: At least 2 more claims (003-4, 006-12) were also true and untraceable to the source list, but they were graded PARTIALLY rather than NOT SUPPORTED, so '8 did not' undercounts; 004-6's Wikipedia citation also broke a second house rule.

claims.claim: Verdict: "84 of 127 cleared on the first pass, and all 3 outright errors were in a date or an attribution rather than an amount."
claims.source: Rounding Errors repository, reports/001-ireland through reports/009-nigeria
claims.passage: "notes": "Independent state-history source (northcarolinahistory.org) gives 2,516, not 2,498; close but not an exact digit match, and the listed source has no URL to verify directly."
claims.notes: 84 of 127 is right; the 'attribution' error is disputed (claim 5), and 004-1 records an amount discrepancy that the 3-error tally does not discuss.

claims.notes: Exhibits 001 to 006 were committed in July 2026, before the second reviewer existed (added 2026-08-01) and before the archived 2026-08-01 fact-checks, so their archived checks came after publishing.

claims.claim: Body: "Exhibit 003 said 2 Chinese provincial admissions followed Liaoning's January 2017 confession within weeks, when both came in January 2018."
claims.source: Rounding Errors repository, reports/003-china
claims.passage: "passage": "Inner Mongolia - January 7, 2018: Authorities disclosed that industrial data for 2016 was inflated by 40 percent" ... "notes": "... this admission was made in January 2018, not within weeks of the January 2017 Liaoning confession."
claims.notes: Both 003 claims 9 and 10 are dated January 2018 in the report.

claims.claim: Body: "Exhibit 007 credited the American promotion of the 10,000-step figure to a Surgeon General in the 1990s, and the only documented Surgeon General walking initiative dates to 2015."
claims.source: Rounding Errors repository, reports/007-10000-steps; cross-checked against src/content/exhibits/007-10000-steps.md and its cited scienceworldreport.com page
claims.passage: Report: "the one well-documented Surgeon General walking initiative (\"Step It Up!\") dates to 2015". Science World Report: "Shape Up America! is a program that was founded in 1994 by Dr. C Everett Koop (a former U.S. Surgeon General)"
claims.notes: The report said 'well-documented', not 'only documented', and the museum's own exhibit 007 now documents a 1994 initiative by a former Surgeon General promoting 10,000 steps, which directly contradicts this sentence.

claims.claim: Body: "Exhibit 001 held 7 of them."
claims.source: Rounding Errors repository, reports/001-ireland
claims.passage: claims 4 to 10: "verdict": "NOT SUPPORTED" with sources "None listed" or a listed notice that "contains neither '26.3%' nor a matching GDP growth figure"
claims.notes: 001 claims 4 to 10 are 7 claims that do not trace to the source list.

claims.claim: Body: the 16 "were confirmed by search corroboration instead of a quoted passage"
claims.source: Rounding Errors repository, reports/003-china and reports/005-scared-straight
claims.passage: "notes": "No URL is provided for this source and independent searches only corroborate the general 'zero tolerance' theme, not the specific 15-case/10-person figures" ... "notes": "... the specific 'unusual, lacked theatrical release' detail could not be verified because both direct fetches of the Hollywood Reporter URL failed (403 then 402 paywall) and search snippets did not reproduce that specific line."
claims.notes: Most of the 16 were corroborated by search, but at least 2 (003-11, 005-11) explicitly were not.

claims.claim: Body: "A reader who followed a citation to the end would have failed to reach the source 16 times"
claims.source: Rounding Errors repository, reports/009-nigeria; CLAUDE.md link-check note
claims.passage: "notes": "Confirmed unchanged from the prior audit: africacheck.org returns 403 to automated fetchers with no Wayback fallback in the sources list, while AfDB does have one. Treated as advisory, not blocking, since the URL is live and presumed accessible to human readers"
claims.notes: Most of the 16 failures were 403 bot walls hit by an automated fetcher, and the reports themselves presume human readers can reach those pages; 1 of the 16 had no URL at all.
